_authoringNotes: WORK_ORDER_1112 -- dungeon runtime balance. Tunable knobs the owner re-tunes in playtest with NO recompile [WO-1331 CORRECTION, 2026-09-02 -- READ THIS BEFORE TRUSTING THE PHRASE ABOVE: 'no recompile' has NEVER meant 'no rebuild'. Assets/Resources IS COMPILED INTO THE PLAYER and LocalJsonCatalogSource resolves Resources FIRST on every platform, so editing this file still costs a full Unity player build (~10 min APK / ~30 min WebGL) before it reaches a device -- and editing the StreamingAssets twin alone changes nothing at all. That is the axis the owner actually cares about, and it is why every past 'move the numbers into JSON' fix did not solve what she was asking for. WO-1331 landed the remote catalog seam (CanonicalJson.Source / RemoteCatalogOverrides) that finally makes a rebuild-free retune possible; it ships FLAG-GATED AND OFF (ff.catalogremote). This file is NOT on the WO-1331 allowlist yet (the seam shipped proven on five catalogs); widening it is a data edit in RemoteCatalogOverrides.Allowlist. See docs/reference/TUNABLE_LEVER_INVENTORY.md section 2.] (loaded via CanonicalJson; the Resources copy wins, StreamingAssets is the desktop source -- keep the two byte-identical). OWNER RULING 2026-08-16, verbatim: 'we should make the lanterns last triple that at minimum or option to dim to extend'. WHAT WAS WRONG: the lantern's only tuning lived as [SerializeField] defaults in Lantern.cs (maxOil 100, oilDrainPerSec 1.6) -- a HIDDEN CODE DEFAULT, the same shape of defect as the 6x storage-repair issue. 100 oil at 1.6/s emptied the flask in 62.5s, and Lantern.IsInDarkness latches at 12% oil, so a composed dungeon went permanently dark ~53s in with the ambush multiplier on, no meter and no visible refill. WHICH KNOB CHANGED AND WHY: oilDrainPerSec 1.6 -> 0.5 (a 3.2x duration increase: 200s to empty, 176s to the darkness latch). CAPACITY WAS DELIBERATELY LEFT AT 100 -- an oil stone tops the flask right off (Lantern.CheckOilStones sets oil = maxOil), so capacity and drain are arithmetically interchangeable for duration, and maxOil is ALSO what the HUD meter's 100% and every oil FRACTION threshold (lowOilFraction 0.25, IsInDarkness 0.12, minOilLightFraction 0.35) are expressed against. Changing the burn RATE moves duration and nothing else; changing capacity would have silently re-scaled what a refill and a meter tick mean. BOTH PIPELINES READ THIS: Lantern.Awake applies these values over the serialized fields, so the hand-built Dungeon_HealersCottage lantern is tripled too. That is intended and is NOT an accidental re-tune -- the cottage scene serialized _maxOil 100 / _oilDrainPerSec 1.6, byte-identical to the code default, i.e. it was never separately tuned and had the exact same 62.5s problem. Keep DungeonLanternBalance's code defaults in step with the values below so an absent file cannot silently reintroduce the 62.5s burn.
